stories.title: The Real Estate Question About Quantum Computing
stories.excerpt: Quantum computing infrastructure is scaling faster than the real estate needed to support it, according to JLL’s “Future of Quantum Real Estate” report. Today, much of the space and infrastructure is concentrated on university campuses. But over the next decade, JLL said it expects the private sector to play a much larger role. Unlike conventional computers, which use bits to process information, quantum computers use qubits to tackle extraordinarily complex problems. The technology won’t replace conventional computing. Instead, JLL described it as “a high-value layer of compute within the digital infrastructure stack.” That emerging layer will require its own physical infrastructure. It could also generate a new real estate niche. Not Your Average Data Center Quantum real estate refers to the facilities that support the research, fabrication and deployment of quantum computing systems. JLL identified more than 240 quantum facilities across nine asset types and 35 countries. It might be tempting to think of quantum real estate as data center 2.0. But the physical requirements are different. Quantum installations can require a “room within a room,” with dilution refrigerators, vibration isolation and electromagnetic shielding alongside conventional computing equipment. Those systems also rely on low-latency fiber connections to the classical computing infrastructure that includes software, networks and data storage systems. The requirements vary further depending on the type of technology involved. JLL discussed several modalities, including topological, silicon spin, photonic, neutral-atom, trapped-ion, and superconducting systems. Each of these offers different potential applications ranging from cybersecurity and telecommunications to pharmaceuticals, logistics and finance. Universities As the Foundation Higher education institutions currently anchor most quantum ecosystems because they bring together specialized talent, government funding, corporate partnerships
bullets: JLL identifies 240+ quantum computing facilities across 9 asset types, 35 countries globally.
Private sector quantum deployment scaling faster than supporting real estate infrastructure available.
Quantum facilities require specialized 'room within room' design with refrigeration, isolation, shielding.
stories.summary: JLL's 'Future of Quantum Real Estate' report identifies an emerging niche: quantum computing infrastructure is outpacing real estate supply. Over 240 quantum facilities exist globally across 9 asset types, concentrated today on university campuses but expected to shift toward private-sector deployment over the next decade. Unlike data centers, quantum installations require specialized physical infrastructure including dilution refrigerators, vibration isolation, and electromagnetic shielding alongside conventional computing equipment.
stories.impact: Minimal near-term relevance to multifamily development. Quantum real estate could generate demand for specialized lab/technical space in select markets with R&D clusters (Boston, San Francisco Bay Area, Austin), but this affects industrial/lab real estate, not residential. Monitor for potential secondary housing demand if major quantum research hubs emerge in new metros, but no direct multifamily supply or financing signal.

stories.title: Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027
stories.excerpt: Tishman Speyer has signed Madewell to a long-term lease for 7,340 square feet at 1 Rockefeller Plaza. Slated to open in 2027, the new store marks Madewell’s first location at Rockefeller Center. Madewell offers premium denim, apparel, and accessories for women and men. Best known for its denim expertise, the brand is recognized for its thoughtful design, innovative approach to denim, and everyday wardrobe essential. The new store will bring the full Madewell experience to life, showcasing the brand’s denim expertise, signature styling, and community-focused programming, according to Tishman Speyer. “Rockefeller Center continues to attract brands that shape culture and consumer behavior globally,” said EB Kelly, Senior Managing Director at Tishman Speyer and Head of Rockefeller Center. “Madewell’s decision to establish a presence here reinforces the Center’s unique ability to combine iconic New York identity with modern cultural relevance.” The post Madewell to Open Its First Rockefeller Center Store in 2027 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Madewell signed 7,340 sq ft lease at 1 Rockefeller Plaza, opening 2027.
Tishman Speyer emphasizes Rockefeller Center's cultural relevance attracting global brands.
Retail tenant expansion signals ongoing Manhattan office/retail mixed-use viability.
stories.summary: Madewell will open its first Rockefeller Center location in 2027, anchoring 7,340 square feet at 1 Rockefeller Plaza under a long-term lease signed by Tishman Speyer. The premium denim and apparel retailer's move signals confidence in Rockefeller Center's ability to attract brands that 'shape culture and consumer behavior globally,' according to Tishman Speyer leadership. The 2027 opening is part of continued retail repositioning at the iconic Manhattan mixed-use property.
stories.impact: Modest signal for NYC multifamily near Midtown. Strong retail tenant commitments at flagship mixed-use centers (Rockefeller Center) support foot traffic, employment density, and urban vibrancy in submarkets surrounding these properties, which can elevate nearby residential appeal. However, this is a single retailer lease—not a structural shift in Manhattan demand. Watch for broader Rockefeller Center or Hudson Yards mixed-use tenant flow to inform Midtown West/Billionaires' Row residential leasing sentiment.

stories.title: NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial has listed 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District for sale, presenting an owner-user opportunity encompassing approximately 99,280 square feet across eight stories. Executive managing director Ryan Campbell, SIOR, and EVP Scott Martin are representing the property. Built in 1924 and currently vacant, 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. features a marble-tile lobby, three Otis traction elevators, including two passenger elevators and one freight elevator, and approximately 300 tons of water-cooled chiller capacity. The building also features emergency power supported by two Generac diesel generators and a fully addressable fire alarm and sprinkler system. “530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. represents a rare opportunity for an owner-user to acquire a substantial office building in one of Pasadena’s most walkable and amenity-rich districts,” said campbell. “The combination of scale, parking, transit access and a central Colorado Boulevard location gives an owner the ability to establish a significant long-term presence in Pasadena while taking advantage of a market where owner-user acquisitions have already reduced available office inventory.” The post NAI Capital Lists Owner-User Opportunity in Pasadena’s Playhouse Village District appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd., Pasadena: 99,280 sq ft, 8-story, built 1924, currently vacant.
Owner-user sale opportunity in walkable Playhouse Village District with parking, transit.
NAI Capital notes owner-user acquisitions already reducing available office inventory locally.
stories.summary: NAI Capital Commercial has listed 530–532 E. Colorado Blvd. in Pasadena's Playhouse Village District for sale, a rare owner-user opportunity spanning 99,280 square feet across eight stories. Built in 1924 and currently vacant, the marble-tile, three-elevator building features 300 tons of water-cooled chiller capacity, dual Generac generators, and full fire/sprinkler systems. The listing broker notes that owner-user acquisitions have already tightened available office inventory in the district.
stories.impact: Indirect signal for Pasadena multifamily demand. Owner-user office acquisitions removing vacancy and stabilizing the Pasadena office market can support employment clustering and local spending that benefits adjacent residential submarkets. However, this is a single distressed asset listing—not a demand surge. More relevant if the trend accelerates and signals office-to-mixed-use conversion opportunities in Playhouse Village or broader Pasadena; monitor for adaptive reuse plays targeting the tech/creative tenants that fill owner-user space.

stories.title: Podcast: How Landlords Can Solve the Tenant Visibility Problem – Sytes’ Rafael Weiss
stories.excerpt: Rafael Weiss is the co-founder of Sytes, a marketplace platform that connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively looking for space in real time. Rafael came to the problem as a developer who lost a deal because tenant demand was invisible until it was too late, and built Sytes to fix the information asymmetry at the core of retail leasing. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Rafael is based in Boca Raton, Florida. bullets: Sytes marketplace connects 350+ tenants, 35,000+ active retail/CRE listings across 50 states.
Platform clients include Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, Dutch Bros; bases in Boca Raton.
Podcast addresses tenant visibility and demand opacity in retail leasing markets.
stories.summary: Sytes, a marketplace platform co-founded by Rafael Weiss, connects commercial real estate landlords, developers, and brokers with tenants actively seeking space in real time. The platform serves nearly 350 tenants and over 35,000 active site listings across all 50 states, with major clients including Kimco, InvenTrust, Church's Chicken, and Dutch Bros. Weiss built Sytes to solve information asymmetry in retail leasing, originating from a deal loss he experienced as a developer.
stories.impact: Peripheral relevance to multifamily. Sytes addresses demand visibility in retail/commercial leasing, not residential. However, improved real-time tenant demand signals can accelerate retail leasing velocity and certainty in mixed-use developments (which often include multifamily), potentially improving financing and IRR assumptions for multifamily+retail projects. Monitor if Sytes expands into residential or if retail velocity improvements boost mixed-use multifamily development economics.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Scoops Up More Miami-Dade Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has bought two more affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, following two acquisitions last week, bringing the total to $115.4 million and 570 units. The investment firm purchased the remaining piece of the Lafayette housing complex in Miami’s Little River neighborhood for $27 million, property records show. Called Lafayette Plaza, the 201,446-square-foot property houses 136 apartments at 155 Northeast 78th Street. The 14-story asset was completed on a 1.1-acre parcel in 2008. CBRE Capital Markets provided a $18.9 million loan, backed by Freddie Mac. Lafayette Plaza is attached to the 160-unit Lafayette Square building, which Starwood purchased for just under $30 million last week. In the second transaction this week, the Miami Beach-based firm purchased another property in Little River, Emerald Terrace, paying $24.6 million. CBRE Capital Markets once again supplied financing: a $17.2 million, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The complex, built in 2009 facing train tracks, houses 124 apartments and a 24,718-square-foot parking garage at 244 and 290 Northwest 72nd Terrace, near the retail center of the neighborhood, where popular restaurants such as Sunny’s Steakhouse are located. In the fourth acquisition, which closed last week, Starwood purchased the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments for $34 million. The 4.8-acre complex, built in 2011, features 20 three-story buildings near the southern end of the county in the Naranja neighborhood. Mansfield, Mass.-based Gatehouse Group developed and sold the four properties. CBRE’s Tim Flint, Jim Flinn and Jon Romano brokered all the recent sales and financings. A representative for Starwood confirmed the transactions. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquired 2 more Miami-Dade affordable housing properties for $51.6M, 260 units.
Total 4-acquisition spree: $115.4M, 570 units; includes Lafayette Plaza (136 units, $27M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units, $24.6M).
Freddie Mac financing; both properties built 2008–2009 in Little River neighborhood.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management has acquired two additional affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County, totaling $51.6 million and 260 units, bringing the firm's recent affordable housing spree to $115.4 million across 570 units. The acquisitions include Lafayette Plaza (136 units at $27M, Freddie Mac loan $18.9M) and Emerald Terrace (124 units at $24.6M, Freddie Mac loan $17.2M), both located in Miami's Little River neighborhood and built in 2008–2009. CBRE Capital Markets arranged Freddie Mac-backed financing for both deals.
stories.impact: Significant capital signal for Miami-Dade multifamily, specifically affordable housing. Starwood's aggressive acquisition pace ($115.4M in affordable units signals confidence in Freddie Mac liquidity and Miami-Dade affordable housing fundamentals amid stabilization of older garden/mid-rise stock. Indicates accessible financing for value-add/stabilized assets with HUD/affordable covenants. Competitive pressure: large institutional buyers consolidating Little River neighborhood inventory may tighten acquisition opportunities for traditional market-rate developers in that submarket. Watch for cap rate compression in Miami-Dade affordable segment and potential spillover demand to adjacent walkable submarkets (Wynwood, Buena Vista).

stories.title: Javits Center Expansion, Tech Upgrades Boosting NYC Hospitality Industry
stories.excerpt: Five years after the Javits Center underwent a $1.5 billion expansion, the Hudson Yards convention venue is continuing to expand its bandwidth to boost its events business and the adjacent New York City hospitality industry. The 3.3 million-square-foot facility recently underwent a $5 million technology upgrade enabling the Javits Center to become the first convention center in the U.S. to provide the newest wireless network, Wi-Fi 7, Commercial Observer can first report. The Wi-Fi 7 system, which debuted last month for Fanatics Fest, provides another competitive edge in attracting more conferences and events going forward, Joyce Leveston, CEO of the Javits Center, told CO. The original Jacob Javits Center opened in 1986. PHOTO: Edmund Vincent Gillon/Museum of the City of New York/Getty Images “So many people who are coming to conventions also want to feel that they can remotely connect with their workplace,” Leveston said on Wednesday, moments before the Javits Center marked its 40th anniversary with a celebration event. “You can’t do that unless you have a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system.” The technology enhancement is just the latest effort by the Javits Center to up the ante in terms of drawing some of the biggest conferences and events to Manhattan and providing a jolt to New York City’s economy. The Javits Center estimates that its convention bookings generated more than 100,000 hotel stays in the New York City region in 2025. The expansion of the Javits Center, which debuted in May 2021, added 1.2 million square feet to the north side of the complex, including a 55,000-square-foot ballroom and a glass-enclosed sustainable rooftop pavilion touted as the largest green roof in the Northeast. The boost to New York City’s hospitality industry from new investments to the Javits Center is evident across the street at 418 11th Avenue, where a new 455-room Hilton-branded hotel is slated to open in the next three years as part of a larger mixed-use project. stories.title: Westphal Company Lands $56M Refi for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Westphal Company has secured $56.1 million in permanent financing for a 354-unit apartment complex in eastern San Diego County. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate financing through the firm’s Fannie Mae platform. The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year term with interest-only payments for the full term. Property records identify Westphal Company owns the Wintercrest Village Apartments, a garden-style community at 12002 Wintercrest Drive in Lakeside, Calif., which is an unincorporated community roughly 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, along with two swimming pools and spas, outdoor courtyards, and fitness rooms. Northmarq’s Aaron Beck, Conor Freeman and Robbie Driscoll facilitated the financing, which allowed Westphal to extract equity from the property while maintaining its cash flow, according to Beck. The lender also waived all operating escrows. “With this Fannie Mae refinance, we were able to unlock trapped equity for the borrower and preserve cash flow while keeping the loan truly non-recourse with no carve-out guarantees,” Beck said in a statement. San Diego’s multifamily market stabilized in the second quarter, with vacancy holding at 5 percent and asking rents rising 0.5 percent to $2,598 per month, according to Northmarq’s second-quarter data. Investment sales slowed roughly 25 percent compared to last year, but median pricing jumped 25 percent to $415,000 per unit. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Westphal Company secured $56.1M refi for 354-unit garden apartment, Lakeside, CA (San Diego County).
Northmarq arranged Fannie Mae fixed-rate, 10-year, interest-only nonrecourse loan; all escrows waived.
Wintercrest Village Apartments: 1–2 bed units, pools, spas, fitness; 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego.
stories.summary: The Westphal Company has refinanced Wintercrest Village Apartments, a 354-unit garden-style community in Lakeside, California (eastern San Diego County), with $56.1 million in permanent Fannie Mae financing. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate, 10-year, nonrecourse loan with interest-only payments and all operating escrows waived. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, two pools, spas, and fitness amenities. The refinance allowed Westphal to extract equity while preserving cash flow.
stories.impact: Positive capital availability signal for San Diego County multifamily. Fannie Mae's appetite for garden-style suburban apartments in Lakeside—20 miles from urban core—with waived escrows and IO terms signals lender confidence in suburban San Diego County rent stability and lease-up. Indicates refinance window remains open for stabilized, non-luxury product; suggests cap rates/leverage acceptable for hold-and-refi strategies. Competitive implication: suburban garden apartments outside San Diego core (i.e., Lakeside, Santee, El Cajon) remain fundable; watch for Fannie Mae issuance trends to gauge whether suburban refi appetite extends to new acquisition/development or remains limited to existing stock.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. If Fortress pursues office-to-residential or office-to-mixed-use conversion at Design Center, it could signal broader South Florida office asset recycling trend. Monitor Jamestown's leasing strategy—if they reposition the property for industrial/flex/last-mile use or mixed-use residential, it would indicate Miami-Dade/Broward County appetite for adaptive reuse. Near-term: no direct multifamily supply or demand signal.
